paragraphs: At our core, we are a global services company. We are the market leader in the highly attractive outsourced maritime health and wellness market, with a market share we estimate exceeds 90%. Over the last 50 years, we have built our leading market position on our depth of staff expertise; broad and innovative service and product offerings; expansive global staff recruitment, training and logistics platforms; global operations infrastructure; and decades-long relationships with cruise line and destination resort partners. Throughout our history, our mission has been simple: helping guests look and feel their best during and after their stay. We serve a critical role for our cruise line and destination resort partners, operating a complex and increasingly important aspect of their overall guest experience. Our decades of investment and know-how have allowed us to construct an unmatched global infrastructure to manage the complexity of our operations. We have consistently expanded our onboard offerings with innovative, leading-edge service and product introductions, and developed powerful staff recruiting, training and logistics platforms, increasingly powered by emerging technologies, including generative and agentic artificial intelligence applications, and global operations infrastructure to manage our operational complexity, maintain our industry-leading quality standards and maximize revenue per health and wellness center. The combination of our renowned recruiting and training platform, deep labor pool, global logistics and supply chain infrastructure and proven revenue management capabilities represents a significant competitive advantage that we believe is not economically feasible to replicate. These competitive advantages served our business well during the recent challenging times for our industry.

The majority of our revenue and profits are earned through long-term agreements with cruise line partners that economically align both parties and contribute to our attractive asset-light financial profile. These agreements range from three to 8.6 years in duration and average approximately five years in length, providing us with the exclusive right to offer health, wellness, aesthetics and fitness services and the ability to sell complementary products onboard the ships we serve. Under these long-term agreements, cruise line partners retain a specified percentage of revenues from all our sales onboard. This inherent alignment encourages collaboration in all aspects of our operations, including facility design, product innovation, pre- and post-cruise sales opportunities, capacity utilization initiatives and other data-driven strategies to drive increased guest traffic and revenue growth. Most of our cruise line agreements encompass 100% of a partner cruise line's existing fleet and all new ships with health and wellness centers introduced by the cruise line during the term of the agreement.

Our cruise line relationships average over 20 years and encompass substantially all of the major global cruise lines, including Carnival Cruise Line, Royal Caribbean Cruises, Princess Cruises, Norwegian Cruise Line, Celebrity Cruises, and Holland America, among many others, as well as recent additions to the industry, such as Virgin Voyages. These partnerships extend across contemporary, premium, luxury and budget cruise lines that operate ships regionally and globally. We maintain what we believe to be an exceptional contract renewal rate with our cruise line partners, having renewed approximately 97% of our contracts based on ship count over the last 15 years, including 100% of our contracts with ships larger than 3,500 berths. We have not only maintained relationships with existing cruise line partners, but also have a history of winning contracts and gaining market share. Since August 2021, we have renewed and extended agreements with existing cruise line partners, including Azamara, Norwegian Cruise Line, for all ships across their three brands, Royal Caribbean Cruises, and Celebrity Cruises. In addition, we have entered into agreements with new cruise line partners, including Adora Cruises, Aroya Cruises, Crystal Cruises, and Mitsui Ocean Cruises. On land, we have longstanding relationships with the world's leading destination hotel and resort operators, including Atlantis, Marriott, Hilton, Caesars Entertainment, Four Seasons, and Mohegan Sun, among others.

Our health and wellness centers operate aboard cruise ships that served over 28 million guests in 2025, seeking to explore and experience our industry-leading health and wellness services and products to complement and enhance their vacation experience. As consumers increasingly incorporate health and wellness activities into their daily lives, they are placing a higher priority on health and wellness services while traveling and vacationing.

Our state-of-the-art health and wellness centers are designed and branded for each cruise line and destination resort partner to optimize their guests' experiences, align with our partners' overall hospitality strategy, and maximize productivity. During the year ended December 31, 2025, our health and wellness centers employed up to 83 highly trained professionals and ranged in size up to over 30,000 square feet, depending on the cruise line or destination resort partner's needs.

We are recognized by our cruise line and destination resort partners and our guests for our comprehensive suite of industry-leading health and wellness services, products and experiences. We curate and deliver a broad range of offerings centered on providing specific health, wellness, aesthetics and fitness solutions to meet our guests' lifestyle routines or objectives. Our services and facilities include: (i) body care, salon, and skin care services and products; (ii) fitness facilities, specialized fitness classes and personal fitness training; (iii) innovative pain management, including acupuncture and light therapies; (iv) body composition analytics and weight loss, systemic detoxification and nutrition regimens; and (v) advanced medi-spa services, including dermal fillers, skin tightening, weight reduction and IV therapies, among others. We offer our guests access to leading aesthetics and wellness brands including ELEMIS®, Grown Alchemist®, Kérastase®, Dysport®, Restylane®, Thermage®, CoolSculpting®, truSculpt® 3D, truSculpt® iD, Good Feet®, Lightstim®, and Hyperice®, among others, with many brands offered exclusively by us in the cruise market. On average, during the year ended December 31, 2025, guests spent approximately $305 per visit. Our solution sales approach drives substantial retail product add on sales to complement our services offerings, with approximately 19% of our revenues derived from the sale of retail products during the year ended December 31, 2025.

We are a Bahamian international business company that earns a substantial portion of our revenue in low- or no-tax jurisdictions, resulting in a comparatively low effective cash tax rate. Additionally, our capital expenditure requirements are comparatively modest, as our cruise line and destination resort partners typically fund the build-out, maintenance, and refurbishment of our health and wellness centers. The combination of our attractive tax rate and asset-light operating model leads to a financial profile that delivers comparatively high cash flow generation.

Historically, with the exception of the adverse impact of the recent COVID-19 pandemic, and since the resumption of our health and wellness center operations on cruise ships and in destination resorts, we have driven strong financial performance and believe our leading market position in a growing industry, differentiated business model, and mutually accretive partnerships with our cruise line and destination resort partners position our business for continued growth. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we achieved Revenues of $961.0 million, Net Income of $71.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $123.3 million.

We operate at the intersection of the historically attractive health and wellness and hospitality and travel industries. We believe we are well-positioned to grow as the hospitality and travel industry continues to expand, with heightened and growing consumer demand for health and wellness services, products, solutions, and experiences while traveling and on vacation.

According to Cruise Lines International Association ("CLIA"), the cruise industry continues to be one of the fastest-growing sectors of tourism. In its 2025 State of the Cruise Industry Report, CLIA reported global passenger volume of approximately 34.6 million ocean-going cruisers globally in 2024, a 6.8% increase from 2019 levels. CLIA noted that global cruise capacity is forecast to continue growing year over year, from approximately 6.3 million passengers in 1995 to an all-time high of 42 million passengers in 2028, representing a compound annual growth rate of 5.8%. This passenger growth has been driven by consistent, significant investments in new, higher value cruise ship capacity; the cost-value differential between vacations at sea and on land; strong loyalty among experienced cruisers; the large and growing appeal of cruising to all demographics, including millennials and Gen-X travelers, who CLIA believes to be the most enthusiastic cruise travelers of the future; and the cruise industry's sustainability and efficiency initiatives, which have been increasingly important to consumers. Many cruise lines offer an increasingly wide range of sustainable shore excursions, including walking, cycling, and paddle or sail experiences, attracting an ever-growing base of health-conscious consumers. The luxury cruise travel market is reported to have tripled since 2010, based on the number of ships offering luxury experiences, and CLIA forecasts that 1.5 million cruise travelers will choose a luxury cruise experience by 2028. According to CLIA, intent to cruise continues to be strong, both among experienced cruisers and potential new cruisers, with 82% of travelers who have cruised indicating that they will cruise again, an increasing number of new-to-cruise travelers choosing vacations at sea, 68% of international travelers considering taking their first cruise, increasing popularity of solo travel, and travel agents reporting higher growth in cruise holidays than any other travel segment, with the highest growth from the premium, luxury and expedition segments.

Our history dates back to our opening the world's first salons at sea onboard transatlantic cruise ships, including the Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth II. For more than 50 years, we have continuously defined and redefined the onboard health, wellness, aesthetics and fitness category by consistently expanding our onboard offerings with innovative and leading-edge service and product introductions, while developing the powerful staff recruiting and training and operational logistics platforms to manage and optimize the complexity of our global operations and maintain our industry-leading quality standards.

As of December 31, 2025, our comprehensive suite of premium health, wellness, aesthetics and fitness services, products, solutions and experiences reached more consumers than ever before, with 206 centers onboard cruise ships addressing a captive audience of over 28 million passengers annually, and 48 destination resort centers serving global travelers at premier destination resorts around the world.

paragraphs: An investment in our securities involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below before making an investment decision. Our business, prospects, financial condition, or operating results could be harmed, and have been harmed, by any of these risks, as well as other risks not currently known to us or that we currently consider immaterial. The trading price of our securities could decline, and has declined, due to any of these risks, and, as a result, you may lose all or part of your investment.

A significant portion of our revenues are generated from our cruise ship health and wellness operations under our long-term agreements with our cruise line partners, which were adversely impacted by the recent pandemic, and could be adversely impacted again in the future by outbreaks of illnesses. Failure to renew our cruise line and destination resort agreements after their expiration date on similar terms or at all could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

In addition, these agreements provide for termination by the cruise lines with limited or no advance notice under certain circumstances, including, among other things, the withdrawal of a ship from the cruise trade, the sale or lease of a ship, or our failure to achieve specified passenger service standards. Termination or nonrenewal of cruise line agreements, either upon completion of their terms or prior thereto, could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition. Some of our land-based destination resort health and wellness center agreements also provide for termination with limited advance notice under certain circumstances.

As a result of the consolidation of the cruise industry, the number of independent cruise lines has decreased in recent years, and this trend may continue. Also, some cruise lines have ceased operating and this may happen to other cruise lines in the future. As a result of these factors, a small number of cruise companies, substantially all of which currently are our customers, dominate the cruise industry.

Prior to the recent pandemic, the cruise industry had never before experienced a complete cessation of its operations. The public concern over the recent pandemic, coupled with a drop in demand for international travel and leisure, and restrictions on international travel and immigration, adversely affected the demand for cruises. In addition, the recent pandemic caused, and future outbreaks of illnesses may cause, some cruise lines to declare bankruptcy or cause their lenders to declare a default, accelerate the related debt, or foreclose on collateral. Such bankruptcies, accelerations or foreclosures could, in some cases, result in the termination of our agreements with certain of our cruise line partners and eliminate our anticipated income and cash flows, which could negatively affect our results of operations. Cruise lines in bankruptcy may not have sufficient assets to pay us termination fees, other unpaid fees, or reimbursements we are owed under their agreements with us. Even if some cruise lines do not declare bankruptcy, they may be unable or unwilling to pay us amounts to which we are entitled on a timely basis or at all. Cruise lines compete for consumer disposable leisure time dollars with virtually all other vacation alternatives. Demand for cruises is dependent on the underlying economic strength

of the countries from which cruise lines source their passengers. Economic changes such as unemployment, economic uncertainty, and the threat of a global recession reduce disposable income or consumer confidence in the countries from which our cruise line partners source their passengers and have affected the demand for vacations, including cruise vacations, which are discretionary purchases.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our audited financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with the information presented in "Selected Historical Financial Information" and our Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included elsewhere in this report. In addition to historical information, the following discussion contains forward-looking statements, such as statements regarding our expectation for future performance, liquidity, and capital resources, that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in or implied by any forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause such differences include those identified below and those described in the sections entitled "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and "Risk Factors." We assume no obligation to update any of these forward-looking statements.
The information for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 is derived from OneSpaWorld's audited Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included elsewhere in this report.
Any reference to "OneSpaWorld" refers to OneSpaWorld Holdings Limited and our consolidated subsidiaries on a forward-looking basis.

OneSpaWorld Holdings Limited ("OneSpaWorld," the "Company," "we," "our, "us" and other similar terms refer to OneSpaWorld Holdings Limited and its consolidated subsidiaries) is the pre-eminent global operator of health and wellness centers onboard cruise ships and a leading operator of health and wellness centers at destination resorts worldwide. We are positioned as a leader in the hospitality-based health and wellness industry. Our highly trained and experienced staff offer guests a comprehensive suite of premium health, wellness, aesthetics and fitness services and products onboard cruise ships and at destination resorts globally. We are the market leader at more than 17x the size of our closest maritime competitor. Over the last 50 years, we have built our leading market position on our depth of staff expertise, broad and innovative service and product offerings, expansive global recruitment, training and logistics platform, as well as decades-long relationships with cruise line and destination resort partners. Throughout our history, our mission has been simple: helping guests look and feel their best during and after their stay.

At our core, we are a global services company. We serve a critical role for our cruise line and destination resort partners, operating a complex and increasingly important aspect of their overall guest experience. Decades of investment and know-how have allowed us to construct an unmatched global infrastructure to manage the complexity of our operations. We have consistently expanded our onboard offerings with innovative and leading-edge service and product introductions, and developed powerful recruiting, training and logistics platforms, increasingly powered by emerging technologies, including generative and agentic artificial intelligence applications, to manage our operational complexity, maintain our industry-leading quality standards, and maximize revenue and profitability per health and wellness center. The combination of our personnel recruiting and training platform, deep proprietary global labor pool, global logistics and supply chain infrastructure, and proven health and wellness center operating, revenue, and profitability management capabilities represents a significant competitive advantage that we believe is not economically feasible to replicate.

A significant portion of our revenues are generated from our cruise ship operations. Historically, we have been able to renew substantially all of our existing cruise line partner agreements and gain new agreements to operate health and wellness centers for new cruise line partners.
In assessing the performance of our business, we consider several key performance indicators used by management. These key indicators include:

• Average Ship Count. The number of ships, on average during the period, on which we operate health and wellness centers. This is a key metric that impacts revenue and profitability and reflects the fact that during the period ships were in and out of service, and is calculated by adding the total number of days that each of the ships generated revenue during the period, divided by the number of calendar days during the period.
• Period End Ship Count. The number of ships at period end on which we operate health and wellness centers. This is a key metric that impacts revenue and profitability.
• Average Ship Count. A key indicator of productivity per ship. Revenue per ship can be affected by the various sizes of health and wellness centers and categories of ships on which we serve.

• Average Weekly Revenue Per Ship. A key indicator of productivity per ship. Revenue per ship can be affected by the various sizes of health and wellness centers and categories of ships on which we serve.

• Average Revenue Per Shipboard Staff Per Day. We utilize this performance metric to assist in determining the productivity of our onboard staff, which we believe is a critical element of our operations.
• Revenue Days. Revenue days are the days on which the health and wellness centers are open onboard a revenue generating cruise with passengers.
• Period End Resort Count. The number of destination resorts at period end on which we operate the health and wellness centers. This is a key metric that impacts revenue and profitability.

paragraphs: 本公司為一間全球性服務公司。我們是高度有吸引力的委外海上健康與 wellness 市場的市場領導者，我們估計市佔率超過 90%。在過去 50 年間，我們透過我們的專業人員深度、廣泛且創新服務與產品組合、擴展的全球員工招募、培訓與物流平台、全球運營基礎設施以及與郵輪線與目的地度假飯店的長期合作關係，建立了我們的領導市場地位。在本公司歷史上，我們的使命一直很簡單：幫助旅客在旅途中與旅後看起來與感覺最好。我們為郵輪線與目的地度假飯店的夥伴扮演關鍵角色，運營他們整體旅客體驗中複雜且越來越重要的部分。我們數十年的投資與專業知識，使我們能夠建立無與倫比的全球基礎設施，以管理我們運營的複雜性。我們持續擴展船上的服務與產品組合，引入創新且領先的服務與產品，並發展強大的員工招募、培訓與物流平台，越來越倚靠新興科技，包括生成式與代理式人工智慧應用，以及全球運營基礎設施，以管理我們的運營複雜性、維持我們的產業領先品質標準並最大化健康與 wellness 中心的收入。我們聞名的招募與培訓平台、深厚的勞動力池、全球物流與供應鏈基礎設施以及已驗證的收入管理能力，代表我們的重大競爭優勢，我們相信這不是經濟上可行的複製對象。這些競爭優勢在最近對產業來說困難的時期中，為我們的業務提供了良好的支持。

我們的收入與利潤主要來自與郵輪線夥伴的長期協議，這些協議在經濟上使雙方對齊，並有助於我們吸引人的輕資產財務結構。這些協議的期限從 3 年到 8.6 年不等，平均約為 5 年，使我們擁有獨家提供健康、 wellness、美容與健身服務的權利，並能在我們服務的船上銷售補充性產品。根據這些長期協議，郵輪線夥伴保留其所有銷售收入的指定百分比。這種內在的對齊促進我們運營各方面的合作，包括設施設計、產品創新、預與後郵輪銷售機會、容量利用率倡議以及其他數據驅動策略，以增加旅客流量與收入成長。我們大多數的郵輪線協議涵蓋了夥伴郵輪線現有船隊的 100%，以及在協議期間郵輪線引入的健康與 wellness 中心的新船。

我們與郵輪線的關係平均超過 20 年，涵蓋了幾乎所有主要的全球郵輪線，包括 Carnival Cruise Line、Royal Caribbean Cruises、Princess Cruises、Norwegian Cruise Line、Celebrity Cruises、Holland America，以及其他許多，以及產業中的新進者，如 Virgin Voyages。這些合作關係橫跨當代、豪華、奢華與經濟型郵輪線，這些線路運營區域與全球的船隻。我們維持我們認為的優異契約續約率與郵輪線夥伴，根據船隻數量，過去 15 年我們續約了約 97% 的契約，包括所有船隻超過 3,500 個牀位的契約。我們不僅維持與現有郵輪線夥伴的關係，而且有贏得契約與增加市佔率的歷史。自 2021 年 8 月以來，我們與現有郵輪線夥伴續約並延長協議，包括 Azamara、Norwegian Cruise Line，為其三個品牌的所有船隻，Royal Caribbean Cruises，以及 Celebrity Cruises。此外，我們與新進的郵輪線夥伴簽訂了協議，包括 Adora Cruises、Aroya Cruises、Crystal Cruises、以及 Mitsui Ocean Cruises。在陸上，我們與全球領先的度假飯店與度假村經營者有長期的合作關係，包括 Atlantis、Marriott、Hilton、Caesars Entertainment、Four Seasons、以及 Mohegan Sun，等等。
本公司健康與 wellness 中心運作於遊輪上，這些遊輪在 2025 年服務過 28 百萬位旅客，旨在探索並體驗本公司領先業界的健康與 wellness 服務與產品，以補充並提升其假期體驗。隨著消費者逐漸將健康與 wellness 活動納入日常生活，他們在旅遊與度假時對健康與 wellness 服務的優先順序也越來越高。
我們的尖端健康與 wellness 中心是為每一家郵輪線與目的地度假村夥伴設計與品牌化，以優化他們旅客的體驗，與夥伴的整體休閒策略對齊，並最大化生產力。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度中，我們的健康與 wellness 中心最多僱用了 83 名高度專業的專業人員，大小則根據郵輪線或目的地度假村夥伴的需求，最多達 30,000 平方英尺。

我們因郵輪線與目的地度假村夥伴以及旅客對我們廣泛的產業領先健康與 wellness 服務、產品與體驗而聞名。我們策劃並提供廣泛的服務與設施，以提供符合旅客生活方式常規或目標的特定健康、 wellness、美容與健身解決方案。我們的服務與設施包括：(i) 身體護理、美髮與皮膚護理服務與產品；(ii) 健身設施、專業健身課程與個人健身訓練；(iii) 創新疼痛管理，包括針灸與光療；(iv) 身體組成分析與減重、系統排毒與營養計畫；以及 (v) 高階醫美服務，包括皮膚填充、皮膚緊致、減重與靜脈注射療法，等等。我們為旅客提供對領先的美容與 wellness 品牌的存取，包括 ELEMIS®、Grown Alchemist®、Kérastase®、Dysport®、Restylane®、Thermage®、CoolSculpting®、truSculpt® 3D、truSculpt® iD、Good Feet®、Lightstim®、以及 Hyperice®，等等，許多品牌在郵輪市場中僅由我們獨家提供。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度中，平均每位旅客每次造訪的消費約為 305 美元。我們的解決方案銷售模式推動了大量的零售產品附加銷售，以補充我們的服務，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度，約有 19% 的收入來自零售產品的銷售。
本公司為巴哈馬國際商業公司，我們在低稅或無稅管轄區賺取了相當大的收入，導致相對較低的有效現金稅率。此外，我們的資本支出需求相對較低，因為我們的郵輪線與目的地度假村夥伴通常資助我們健康與 wellness 中心的建設、維護與翻新。我們的吸引人的稅率與輕資產運營模式結合，導致財務結構能產生相對較高的現金流。

歷史上，除了最近 COVID-19 大流行造成的不利影響外，自我們在郵輪與目的地度假村恢復健康與 wellness 中心運營以來，我們已實現強勁的財務表現，我們相信我們在成長產業中的領導市場地位、差異化的商業模式以及與郵輪線與目的地度假村夥伴的互利合作，為我們的業務帶來持續成長的潛力。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度，我們實現了營收 961.0 百萬美元、淨收入 71.6 百萬美元以及調整後 EBITDA 123.3 百萬美元。
我們運作於歷史來看具吸引力的健康與 wellness 行業以及旅館與旅遊產業的交會點。我們認為我們處於一個有利的立場，可以隨著旅館與旅遊產業持續擴張而成長，同時消費者對旅行與度假時的健康與 wellness 服務、產品、解決方案與體驗的需求持續增加。

根據 Cruise Lines International Association（"CLIA"），遊輪產業持續為旅遊業中成長最快的部門之一。在其 2025 年遊輪產業報告中，CLIA 報告 2024 年全球海洋遊輪乘客數量約為 34.6 百萬，較 2019 年水平增加 6.8%。CLIA 指出，全球遊輪載客量預期將持續每年成長，從 1995 年約 6.3 百萬乘客增至 2028 年的歷史高點 42 百萬乘客，代表年複合成長率為 5.8%。這項乘客成長是由於持續且大量的投資於新、高價值遊輪船隻容量；海上假期與陸地假期的費用與價值差異；經驗豐富遊輪乘客的強烈忠誠度；以及遊輪產業對所有世代，包括千禧世代與 Gen-X 旅客的廣大吸引力，CLIA 認為這些是未來最熱衷遊輪旅行的族羣；以及遊輪產業的可持續性與效率倡議，這對消費者而言越來越重要。許多遊輪線提供越來越廣泛的可持續性岸上活動，包括步行、騎自行車、劃槳或帆船體驗，吸引越來越多重視健康的消費者。根據 CLIA 的報告，豪華遊輪旅行市場自 2010 年以來已成長三倍，根據提供豪華體驗的船隻數量計算，CLIA 預測到 2028 年將有 1.5 百萬遊輪旅客選擇豪華遊輪體驗。根據 CLIA，遊輪意圖持續強勁，不僅在經驗豐富的遊輪旅客與潛在新旅客之間，有 82% 的旅客表示他們會再次遊輪，越來越多新旅客選擇海上假期，68% 的國際旅客考慮第一次搭乘遊輪，單人旅行的流行度增加，以及旅行社報告指出遊輪假期的成長率高於任何其他旅遊類型，其中成長最快的為豪華、豪華與探險類型。

我們的歷史可以追溯到我們在跨大西洋遊輪船上開設世界上第一間海上的美髮廳，包括 Queen Mary 和 Queen Elizabeth II。在超過 50 年的時間裡，我們持續定義並重新定義 onboard 的健康、wellness、美學與健身類別，透過不斷擴展 onboard 的服務與產品，引入創新且領先的服務與產品，同時建立強大的員工招募與培訓以及運營物流平台，以管理並優化我們全球運營的複雜性，並維持我們業界領先的品質標準。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的全面性高階健康、wellness、美學與健身服務、產品、解決方案與體驗已觸及前所未有的消費者數量，有 206 個中心設置在遊輪船上，服務每年超過 28 百萬名乘客，並有 48 個目的地度假中心服務全球旅客於世界各地的豪華度假勝地。
• 服務與產品的持續創新，搭配增強的諮詢式銷售培訓技巧，導致收入組成向高價值附加與高價服務、高價產品以及與旅客服務相關的產品購買高附加率轉變；
• 增強並擴展與遊輪線與目的地度假中心夥伴的合作關係；

paragraphs: 下列對我們經審計財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本報告中「選取歷史財務資訊」及我們的合併財務報表及其附註所載資訊一併閱讀。除歷史資訊外，下列討論包含前瞻性陳述，例如關於我們對未來表現、流動性及資本資源的預期，這些陳述涉及風險、不確定性及假設，可能導致實際結果與任何前瞻性陳述所載或暗示之內容有重大差異。導致此等差異的因素包括下列所識別者，以及「對前瞻性陳述的警示聲明」及「風險因素」節所述者。我們不承擔更新任何這些前瞻性陳述的義務。
2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日年度的資訊係根據OneSpaWorld經審計的合併財務報表及其附註所載資訊擷取。
任何提及「OneSpaWorld」之參考係指OneSpaWorld Holdings Limited及其合併子公司，以前瞻性為基礎。

OneSpaWorld Holdings Limited（「OneSpaWorld」、「本公司」、「我們」、「我們的」、「我們」及其他類似用語，均指OneSpaWorld Holdings Limited及其合併子公司）為全球首屈一指的健康與 wellness 中心營運商，專營於郵輪上，並為全球目的地度假村的健康與 wellness 中心領導營運商。我們在以酒店為基礎的健康與 wellness 行業中定位為領導者。我們高度訓練且經驗豐富的員工為旅客提供全面的高級健康、 wellness、美容及健身服務與產品，於郵輪上及全球目的地度假村。我們在市場上為規模超過最接近的海上競爭對手17倍的領導者。在過去50年中，我們透過員工專業知識的深度、廣泛且創新服務與產品的提供、廣泛的全球招募、培訓與物流平台，以及與郵輪線與目的地度假村夥伴長達數十年的關係，建立了領導市場地位。在整個歷史中，我們的使命簡單明確：協助旅客在旅途中及旅後看起來與感覺最佳。

我們的核心為一全球服務公司。我們為郵輪線與目的地度假村夥伴扮演關鍵角色，營運其整體旅客體驗中複雜且日益重要的方面。數十年的投資與專業知識使我們得以建立無與倫比的全球基礎設施，以管理我們營運的複雜性。我們持續擴展船上的服務，透過創新且領先的服務與產品推出，並發展強大的招募、培訓與物流平台，日益透過新興科技，包括生成式與代理式人工智慧應用，以管理我們營運的複雜性，維持我們行業領先的品質標準，並最大化每間健康與 wellness 中心的收入與利潤。我們的人力招募與培訓平台、深厚的專屬全球勞動力池、全球物流與供應鏈基礎設施，以及已驗證的健康與 wellness 中心營運、收入與利潤管理能力的組合，代表我們認為難以經濟上複製的重大競爭優勢。
我們收入的很大一部分來自於郵輪營運。歷史上，我們能夠續約我們現有郵輪線夥伴契約的絕大部分，並獲得與新郵輪線夥伴簽訂新契約以營運健康與 wellness 中心。
在評估我們業務的表現時，我們考量管理層使用的幾個關鍵績效指標。這些關鍵指標包括：
• 平均船隻數。我們於期間平均營運健康與 wellness 中心的船隻數。這是影響收入與利潤的關鍵指標，反映期間船隻進出服務的情況，並計算為將期間內每艘船產生收入的總天數相加，除以期間內的總曆史天數。
• 期末船隻數。期末時本公司經營健康與 wellness 中心的船隻數量。此為影響營業收入與獲利的重要指標。
• 平均船隻數。為衡量每艘船生產力的重要指標。每艘船的營業收入可能受健康與 wellness 中心規模及服務船隻類別的影響。
• 平均每週每艘船營業收入。為衡量每艘船生產力的重要指標。每艘船的營業收入可能受健康與 wellness 中心規模及服務船隻類別的影響。
• 平均每艘船每名船員每日營業收入。本公司利用此績效指標協助評估 onboard 員工的生產力，我們認為這是本公司運營的重要要素。
• 營業日數。營業日數為健康與 wellness 中心在載有乘客的營業航次船隻上開放營運的天數。
• 期末度假村數。期末時本公司經營健康與 wellness 中心的度假村數量。此為影響營業收入與獲利的重要指標。

paragraphs: 投資本公司證券涉及高度風險。您在做出投資決定前應謹慎考慮下列所描述的風險。本公司業務、前景、財務狀況或營運成果可能受這些風險影響，且已受這些風險影響，以及其它尚未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之風險。本公司證券之交易價格可能下跌，且已下跌，係因這些風險所致，因此您可能損失全部或部分投資。
我們營收的相當大一部分來自於我們與遊輪線業者簽訂之長期契約所產生之遊輪船健康與 wellness 運營業務，而這些業務因近期疫情而受到負面影響，未來亦可能因疾病爆發而再次受到負面影響。若在契約到期後無法以相同條件或任何條件續約，將對本公司業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大負面影響。
此外，這些契約允許遊輪線在特定情況下，以有限或無預先通知的方式終止契約，包括但不限於船隻退出遊輪航線、船隻出售或租賃，或本公司未能達成指定之乘客服務標準。契約終止或未續約，無論是在契約到期後或到期前，均可能對本公司業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大負面影響。部分我們陸上目的地度假中心健康與 wellness 中心契約亦允許在特定情況下以有限預先通知終止契約。
由於遊輪產業的合併，近年來獨立遊輪線的數量已減少，且此趨勢可能持續。此外，部分遊輪線已停止營運，未來可能有其他遊輪線也停止營運。因此，少數遊輪公司，幾乎全部為本公司客戶，目前主宰遊輪產業。

在近期疫情之前，遊輪產業從來未經歷過完全停止營運的情況。近期疫情所引發的公眾憂慮，加上國際旅遊與休閒需求下降，以及國際旅遊與移民限制，已對遊輪需求造成負面影響。此外，近期疫情導致，未來若疾病爆發，也可能導致部分遊輪線聲請破產，或其貸款人宣告違約、加速相關債務或對擔保品進行拍賣。這些破產、債務加速或拍賣，可能導致某些遊輪線與我們簽訂之契約終止，並消除我們預期之收入與現金流，進而對我們營運結果造成負面影響。破產之遊輪線可能無法支付我們契約終止費用、其他未付費用或應由其支付之補償金額。即使某些遊輪線未聲請破產，也可能無法或不願按時或完全支付我們應得之金額。遊輪線與幾乎所有其他休閒旅遊替代方案競爭消費者可支配休閒預算。對遊輪需求的依賴取決於遊輪線來源乘客國家的經濟強度
遊輪線來源乘客國家的經濟變化，如失業率、經濟不確定性以及全球經濟衰退的威脅，會降低這些國家的可支配所得或消費者信心，並已影響到度假需求，包括遊輪度假，這些屬於非必要性消費。
